Subject: INTERNAL - Enterprisecorp procurement exception request (SLA + discount)

Team —

Following the discovery/demo, Enterprisecorp (Deal RDW-ENT-2026-042) is asking for two non-standard items that will require internal approvals: 

1) SLA: 99.95% uptime (ours default commercial SLA is 99.9%). Procurement says VP Finance must approve higher SLA.
2) Discount: 20% off list for the first 12-month committed term (they've signaled price sensitivity and aggressive CIO timeline). Our pricing guardrails allow up to 15% at Director level; >15% requires exec approval.

Why approve? Strategic reasons: 
- Anchor customer in a key US enterprise vertical with high upsell potential (embedding inference into multiple product lines).
- Fast decision window (CIO expects vendor recommendation by 30-Jun); losing time here risks them choosing a competitor.
- Enterprisecorp will commit to a 12-month reserved capacity SKU which gives predictable revenue and utilization.

Risks/mitigations: 
- SLA exposure: we can limit the 99.95% SLA to core revenue-generating routes (exclude experimental APIs) and include standard cap on credits. Legal (Hannah) — can you propose limiting language and credit caps?
- Discount: propose a performance-based clause (discount applies first 3 months; thereafter re-evaluate against usage milestones) — keeps upside if they scale.

Docs attached: SOW draft and Redwood procurement exceptions form (filled).

Ask: Aditya — can you approve up to 20% as a one-time exception for this deal given the strategic upside? Hannah — can you weigh in on limiting SLA exposure / contract language so we can present a clean ask to Procurement/Vice President?

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: INTERNAL - Enterprisecorp procurement exception request (SLA + discount)

Marissa / team —

I reviewed the SOW and exception form. High-level thoughts: 
- SLA: I can approve routing the 99.95% ask to VP Finance with a recommended mitigation: limit the 99.95% to Production inference endpoints supporting the core product (explicitly exclude non-prod and beta routes). Cap service credit at 10% of monthly fees for SLA breaches and require 30-day cure periods. That should limit financial exposure.
- Discount: 20% is above our standard, but given the reserved capacity commitment and the strategic nature, I'm comfortable supporting an exec-level ask if we bind certain commercial protections: minimum committed spend for first 3 months and milestone-based review at month 6. Also require that the discount cliffs back to standard pricing if they fail to meet usage thresholds.

I can draft redlines for the SOW and a short internal memo for VP Finance summarizing exposure and proposed guardrails.

Hannah
General Counsel (Commercial Contracts) | Redwood Inference
